entries.source: SDK 26.2, MPMediaPlaylist.h, MP_EXTERN NSString * const MPMediaPlaylistPropertySeedItems; and @property (nonatomic, readonly, nullable) NSArray<MPMediaItem *> *seedItems MP_API(ios(8.0))
entries.reason: read CLASS-SCOPED with tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua over the armv7 cache of 6.1.3, MPMediaPlaylist is PRESENT with 15 own instance methods - -count, -encodeWithCoder:, -existsInLibrary, -hash, -initWithCoder:, -initWithPersistentID:, -isEqual:, -items, -loadGeniusMixArtworkWithTileLength:completionBlock:, -mediaTypes, -name, -persistentID, -playlistAttributes, -representativeItem and -valueForProperty: - and -seedItems is in none of them, while -valueForProperty: IS one of them. Across all 11378 classes of the whole 6.1.3 cache exactly zero declare -seedItems, so no category in any framework supplies it either. What makes the row carryable is that the accessor the property is a convenience over is the RELEASE'S OWN: the header declares it as a named key, MPMediaPlaylistPropertySeedItems, beside the property, and -valueForProperty: is the one accessor that takes such a key. The key shadows nothing, and that was checked rather than assumed: 6.1.3 exports none of MediaPlayer's 36 constants so the port carries this one, and the declaration in MPMediaPlaylist.h carries NO MP_API annotation at all while the two 9.3 keys beside it carry MP_API(ios(9.3)) - an unannotated extern is unversioned, so the name is not something a later release introduced. THE KEY'S VALUE WAS READ, NOT DERIVED, because the port's convention that these values equal the property's own name is FALSE for the two keys beside it - MPMediaPlaylistPropertyAuthorDisplayName is 'externalVendorDisplayName' and MPMediaPlaylistPropertyDescriptionText is 'descriptionInfo', neither of which is the name of the constant or of the property - so a value spelled from this key's name would have been a guess dressed as a fact. Read from Apple's own framework: it is 'seedItems'. So for THIS key the convention holds and that is a fact about this key, not a rule; one of the three holds its own name. THE TYPE IS THE CONTENT OF THE METHOD: -valueForProperty: returns id and the header declares nullable NSArray<MPMediaItem *> *, so a value of the wrong type is refused rather than forwarded, at two levels - the container must be an NSArray and every element an MPMediaItem. Removing the container test does not turn the check RED, it makes it CRASH: '-[__NSCFConstantString countByEnumeratingWithState:objects:count:]: unrecognized selector', because the caller then sends an array message to whatever the release held under the key
entries.effect: a caller reads the seed items the release holds under MPMediaPlaylistPropertySeedItems - the Genius items a generated playlist was made from - and reads nil when the release holds nothing there, when what it holds is not an array, or when any element of that array is not an MPMediaItem. An empty array is answered as an empty array, not as nil

entries.source: SDK 26.2, MPMediaPlaylist.h, MP_INIT_UNAVAILABLE; - (instancetype)initWithName:(NSString *)name NS_DESIGNATED_INITIALIZER; @property (nonatomic, readonly, copy) NSString *name; @property (null_resettable, nonatomic, copy) NSString *authorDisplayName; @property (nonatomic, copy) NSString *descriptionText;
entries.reason: read CLASS-SCOPED with tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua over the armv7 caches of 6.1.3 and 4.3, this class reads ABSENT from both, with the controls the MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption row records - the same reader, the same files, MPNowPlayingInfoCenter PRESENT at 6.1.3 and ABSENT at 4.3. New code, so nothing to shadow. It is a value holder: the header gives it one designated initializer and three properties and no behaviour. NULL_RESETTABLE IS THE PART THAT IS A CONTRACT RATHER THAN AN ATTRIBUTE, and it is honoured: the header's own comment says authorDisplayName 'Defaults to the requesting app's display name', so nil does not mean 'no author' but 'not set, use the app's name', and the getter therefore answers the main bundle's own display name and never nil. The lookup is real and its fallback chain is three deep - CFBundleDisplayName, then CFBundleName, then -[NSProcessInfo processInfo] processName - and the third step exists because a MEASUREMENT demanded it: the host check is a bare command-line binary whose Info.plist carries neither key, and a first draft that answered nil there put two lines RED, the 'never set' case and the 'reset to nil' case. null_resettable promises an answer for nil, so a getter that can return nil breaks its own promise. NOT -[NSBundle bundleName], which the first draft used: it is macOS-only, the iOS SDK declares no such selector, and clang answered 'no visible @interface for NSBundle declares the selector bundleName'. MP_INIT_UNAVAILABLE is compile-time (MediaPlayerDefines.h:70-73), so no -init is declared and the header's designated initializer is the only way in
entries.effect: NSClassFromString answers the class and a caller-built object holds the name it was created under, copied and readonly, plus a descriptionText it may set; authorDisplayName reads the requesting app's own display name when it was never set, which is what the header's null_resettable promises, and reads back exactly what a caller set otherwise
